claims.text: Overall high-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings is governed by formation of a controlled, adherent oxide scale.
The oxide scale stabilizes the coating surface microstructure against high-temperature softening.
The oxide scale stabilizes the coating against grain-boundary sliding.
Pre-oxidation should reduce wear relative to an as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating.
As-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coatings produced by physical vapor deposition may have a nanocrystalline or columnar microstructure.
Annealing in air at 500°C for 1 hour will promote formation of a continuous, controlled surface oxide scale.
The pre-oxidation scale will be a mixed oxide containing oxides of Fe, Ni, Cr, Co, and possibly Cu.
The mixed oxide scale will enhance surface hardness.
The mixed oxide scale will act as a thermal barrier.
Controlled pre-oxidation will form a protective, adherent scale that limits further oxidation.
Limiting further oxidation will suppress high-temperature softening of the coating.
Pre-oxidation will reduce grain-boundary mobility and thereby mitigate grain-boundary sliding under high-temperature loading.
Grain-boundary sliding is typically accelerated under high-temperature loading.
At 500–700°C in ambient-air sliding wear, a pre-oxidized coating will have a lower wear rate than the as-deposited baseline.
At 500–700°C in ambient-air sliding wear, a pre-oxidized coating will exhibit a more stable coefficient of friction than the as-deposited baseline.
An intact and uniform oxide scale will remain detectable during and after high-temperature wear testing of the pre-oxidized coating.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply approximately from 500°C to 700°C under sliding wear in ambient air.
The benefit of pre-oxidation may be lost when the oxide scale degrades, becomes excessively thick, or spalls.
The benefit of pre-oxidation may be lost under extremely severe wear loads.
